items.claim: The default proto codec now asserts on the APIv2 `proto.Message` (requires `ProtoReflect()`), so APIv1-only messages (gogo/protobuf, pre-1.4 protoc-gen-go output) that the old `github.com/golang/protobuf/proto` path accepted are rejected in both Marshal and Unmarshal (line 49).
items.consequence: A service whose request/response types only implement Reset/String/ProtoMessage makes any RPC: Marshal returns `failed to marshal, message is *T, want proto.Message` and the RPC fails. Confirmed with a scratch overlay test using `reflection/grpc_testing_not_regenerate.SearchRequestV3`: both Marshal and Unmarshal return this error at head. Fix: adapt with `protoadapt.MessageV2Of` for `protoadapt.MessageV1` inputs.

items.claim: `Details()` now returns whatever `any.UnmarshalNew()` yields, which for legacy APIv1-only message types is the protobuf-internal `*impl.messageIfaceWrapper` rather than the concrete type that `ptypes.DynamicAny` used to return.
items.consequence: A caller attaches a legacy-generated detail with `WithDetails(&pb.Legacy{})` and later does `d.(*pb.Legacy)` (or a type switch) over `st.Details()`: the assertion silently fails. Confirmed with a scratch test: the detail comes back as `*impl.messageIfaceWrapper` and the concrete assertion is false. The returned value also no longer satisfies the v1 `proto.Message` interface for such types. Fix: convert with `protoadapt.MessageV1Of(detail)` before appending.

items.claim: The result of `rInterval.CheckValid()` is discarded and the error message formats the outer `err` from `stream.Recv()`, which is always nil at this point.
items.consequence: An LRS server sends a first LoadStatsResponse with a missing or invalid `load_reporting_interval`: the returned error reads `invalid load_reporting_interval: <nil>`, losing the actual reason (nil Duration, out of range, mismatched sign) that the old `ptypes.Duration` error carried.

items.claim: `ClientMessage.toProto` and `ServerMessage.toProto` (line 282) now assert on the APIv2 `proto.Message`, so APIv1-only messages fall through to the 'neither proto.message nor []byte' branch.
items.consequence: A server using a custom or gogo codec with v1-only message types has binary logging enabled: each client/server message entry is logged with empty payload data and only an Info line, where previously the payload was marshalled and recorded.

items.claim: The conflict resolution downgrades `golang.org/x/tools` from v0.17.0 to v0.14.0 (and `golang.org/x/sync` 0.6.0 to 0.4.0 in go.sum, plus a new `x/sys v0.13.0` indirect), which is unrelated to the protobuf migration.
items.consequence: `vet.sh` and CI install goimports from `test/tools` and now get the older x/tools, reverting the bump already on main (5051eeae 'Update go mod'). Formatting and vet results can differ from main, and the next dependency-update PR has to redo the bump.

items.claim: `convertDuration` now returns `d.AsDuration(), d.CheckValid()`, which accepts durations that overflow `time.Duration` and returns a non-zero value alongside an error.
items.consequence: An RLS config sets `lookup_service_timeout` to `10000000000s` (valid per `CheckValid`'s ±10000-year range but above the ~292-year `time.Duration` limit): `ptypes.Duration` used to reject it with 'out of range for time.Duration', so config parsing failed. Now `AsDuration` silently saturates to `math.MaxInt64` and the config is accepted with an effectively infinite timeout.

items.claim: The v1 branch of `ToJSON` now goes through `protojson`, which marshals a typed-nil message as `{}`, whereas `jsonpb` returned an error ('Marshal called with nil') and fell back to `%+v`.
items.consequence: `pretty.ToJSON(resp)` with a typed-nil proto pointer (e.g. `var s *spb.Status`) now logs `{}`, indistinguishable from an empty message; the scratch test at head confirmed the `{}` output. Before, the fallback printed `<nil>`, so debug logs of nil responses or configs become misleading.

items.claim: After the change the `protov1.Message` and `protov2.Message` cases are near-identical `protojson` marshalling blocks, and the file still imports the deprecated `github.com/golang/protobuf/proto` solely for `MessageV2`.
items.consequence: Maintenance cost: two duplicated branches (differing only in an implied `Multiline`) plus a remaining dependency on the package this PR is removing. A single helper that converts via `protoadapt.MessageV2Of` and marshals once would remove both the duplication and the old import.

items.claim: The test builds its expected error with `protoimpl.X.NewError("invalid empty type URL")`, importing `google.golang.org/protobuf/runtime/protoimpl` (documented as for generated code only) and pinning the protobuf library's internal error text.
items.consequence: `equalError` compares `.Error()` strings, so any wording change in a future protobuf-go release breaks `TestStatus_ErrorDetails_Fail` although gRPC behaviour is unchanged. Asserting only that the element is a non-nil `error` would avoid the `protoimpl` dependency and the brittle string match.
